market_summary: Markets are in a risk-on mood heading into Q3 earnings season: Tesla's Q3 delivery beat (486,532 vs ~461k expected) sent the stock up 5% on 2-Oct, Nvidia is pushing toward fresh record highs on AI/cloud capex optimism, and Meta is expanding its enterprise AI push (Muse agent, new enterprise platform). US megacaps (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL) report later in October and analysts expect that to be a catalyst for further S&P 500 gains. In Singapore, the STI has had a soft week (-0.6% Friday) with SGX itself the standout mover — down 7.2% on the day and 16% over the month on unusually heavy volume (4.3x normal), while SIA/Scoot's Middle East flight cancellations have been extended into December, adding to weak travel-sector sentiment.

picks.thesis: Q3 deliveries beat consensus by ~24.5k units and the stock already popped 5% on the news; momentum plus an upcoming Oct 21 earnings date gives a clear near-term catalyst window. Price is back above its 50-day MA (+7.1%) after a rough 3-month stretch, suggesting a potential trend reversal off depressed levels (still -24% from 52w high).
picks.news: Tesla Q3 2026 deliveries of 486,532 vehicles beat expectations by ~24,558 units; shares up 5% on 2-Oct-2026. Energy storage missed forecasts. Earnings scheduled Oct 21.
picks.risks: Energy storage miss shows not all segments are strong; stock has very high volatility (46%) and beta (1.83), so gains can reverse quickly; margin/pricing questions remain into the Oct 21 print.

picks.thesis: Nvidia is nearing its first record high since May as AI/cloud capex spending stays strong; analyst consensus sees ~40% upside and sentiment is overwhelmingly bullish (58 buy/2 hold/1 sell). Price is already running above both 50-day (+7.1%) and 200-day (+16.5%) moving averages, indicating a confirmed uptrend ahead of big tech earnings that should reinforce the AI capex narrative.
picks.news: 2-Oct-2026 Yahoo Finance piece notes Nvidia, TSMC and Broadcom could benefit from strong cloud/AI spending results; stock is approaching a new high not seen since May.
picks.risks: High beta (1.59) and rich valuation (any disappointment in upcoming megacap cloud capex commentary could trigger a sharp pullback); stock has already run up materially over 3/6 months, leaving less room for surprise.

picks.thesis: Meta is pushing further into enterprise AI (Muse agent expansion to small businesses, new enterprise platform led by an ex-MongoDB CEO), a concrete monetization angle beyond its core ad business. The stock is up 22.6% in the last month and trading well above both 50-day (+16.3%) and 200-day (+15.7%) averages, showing strong momentum into Q3 earnings season.
picks.news: 2-Oct-2026: Meta launched an enterprise AI platform and is expanding its Muse AI agent to small businesses with Shopify/Slack/QuickBooks integrations, its clearest commercial AI push yet.
picks.risks: Very high volatility (41.8%) and beta (1.3); stock already +26.5% over 6 months so good news may be partly priced in; past AI-team churn (background item) signals execution risk in AI strategy.

picks.thesis: Singapore Exchange fell 7.2% in a single session on 4.3x normal volume, extending a -16% one-month and -13% three-month decline — a sharp, high-volume breakdown that often signals continued near-term weakness or a negative structural development not yet reflected in slower-moving analyst targets (which still imply +16.6% upside). Price is now 12.8% below its 50-day average, confirming a broken short-term trend.
picks.news: Price data shows SGX dropped 7.2% on 2-Oct-2026 with rel_volume_20d of 4.35x; no specific company news was found in available sources, but the move is large enough to warrant caution on long exposure.
picks.risks: No confirmed news catalyst was found for the drop — it could be a one-off overreaction (e.g., index rebalancing, large block trade) that reverses quickly; analyst consensus remains bullish, so a snap-back rally is a real risk if the move proves technical rather than fundamental.

picks.thesis: Singapore Airlines/Scoot have extended Middle East flight cancellations through December, prolonging a revenue headwind on top of an already weak chart: -13.7% over 3 months, trading below both 50-day and 200-day averages, with 4 of 13 analysts rating it a sell (the most bearish skew on this watchlist).
picks.news: 24-Sep-2026: SIA and Scoot extended Middle East flight cancellations to December 2026 due to regional tensions.
picks.risks: News is over a week old and may already be priced in; any easing of Middle East tensions or strong travel demand into year-end holiday season could quickly reverse the stock's underperformance; low beta (0.64) limits downside speed.
